source_excerpts.text:
I derived a way to certify a macroscopic transport improvement in an interacting quantum chain using only a local energy-detuning statistic—not the equilibrium distribution, partition function, or a reconstructed many-body state.
The result changes the information interface rather than contradicting the earlier lower bound. It uses controlled local preparations and a specified physical dephasing model. Its central mathematical step is an exact treatment of undamped populations, which prevents a transport certificate from concealing an unknown global relaxation time.
The completed derivation includes the infinite-system, long-time second-moment limit. It is not merely a finite-cluster calculation or a large-noise approximation. However, historical novelty, independent proof validation, and superiority over the strongest specialised computational methods remain unestablished. The broader high-precision prediction capability is still open.

The previous rare-information obstruction survives a decision-only reformulation. Place a decision threshold between the two modified-system expectations in the earlier construction: a successful decision procedure must still distinguish the nearly identical reference states. Asking for one bit instead of a precise expectation does not automatically eliminate the acquisition cost.    research_note
I therefore examined three different routes: equilibrium decision certificates, observable-specific dynamical residuals, and transport certificates built around the distinction between populations and coherences.
The first route already has substantial prior art: certified equilibrium algorithms can return rigorous observable intervals without reconstructing the entire state. The unresolved issue is affordable convergence in the difficult regimes—not inventing the idea of an interval certificate. [Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51592-3)
The second route fails when a small residual is converted into an error bound by dividing by an unknown relaxation rate. Separating Hamiltonian evolution from a degenerate dissipator is also established in quantum hypocoercivity; that separation alone is not a new principle. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.11503v2)
The productive route was more specific:
Enforce the undamped population constraints exactly

source_excerpts.text:
For an imaginary-antisymmetric witness \(f\) obeying
\[ \boxed{PAf=0} \]
and a real-symmetric witness \(g\), define
\[ \begin{aligned} L(f) &= 2\langle J,f\rangle-\langle f,Sf\rangle -\langle Af,S^+Af\rangle,\\ U(g) &= \langle J-Ag,S_{\mathrm{odd}}^{-1}(J-Ag)\rangle +\langle g,Sg\rangle . \end{aligned} \]
Then
\[ L(f)/n\le\kappa_n\le U(g)/n. \]
More importantly, their difference is exactly computable:
\[ \boxed{ U(g)-L(f) = \|Sf-(J-Ag)\|_{S^+}^{\,2} + \|Sg+Af\|_{S^+}^{\,2}. } \]
This is a certificate, not an error estimate divided by an unknown relaxation time.
The underlying symmetric/skew variational reasoning has precedent in nonreversible Dirichlet principles. The contribution being investigated is its explicit constrained implementation and consequences for this physical task, not a claim to have invented variational response theory. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.2445)
Given an approximate off-diagonal witness \(g_0\), the required diagonal correction \(\phi\) solves
\[ M\phi=-b, \qquad M=-PA S_{\mathrm{odd}}^{-1}AP. \]
For hopping amplitudes \(t_e\),
\[ \boxed{ (M\phi)(\eta) = \frac{2}{d} \sum_{e=\{i,j\}}t_e^2 \big[\phi(\eta)-\phi(\eta^{ij})\big]. } \]
This is a classical exclusion-process Laplacian.
It is an exact static constraint operator—not an assertion that the quantum dynamics has become classical. The diagonal interactions disappear from this particular constraint equation because they commute with \(\phi\), not because their dynamical effects are neglected.
There is also a constructive representation advantage. Exchanges preserve the degree of a diagonal monomial \(Z_C=\prod_{i\in C}Z_i\). A source of degree at most \(p\) can therefore be corrected in a space of dimension
\[ N_p=\sum_{k=0}^{p}\binom nk. \]
For fixed \(p\), exact rational solution and verification have polynomial cost in \(n\) and the input bit length.
The remaining difficulty is not hidden: I have not proved that high-accuracy transport always admits a small \(p\) or a compact off-diagonal witness.
Dropping the balance constraint gives a false positive even for
\[ S=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}, \qquad A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}, \qquad J=(1,0). \]
The true response is zero. An inadmissible trial that simply discards its undamped residual produces a purported lower bound of one.
This is why exact balance is load-bearing rather than optional numerical

source_excerpts.text:
elementary cosine bounds imply
\[ \Xi\le \frac{2(1-e^{d\tau}\mu)}{c\tau^2}. \]
For \(N\) independent preparations and sample mean \(\bar X\), use
\[ h=\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2/\alpha)}{N}} \]
to obtain the confidence-valid bound
\[ \boxed{ \Xi_U= \frac{2[1-e^{d\tau}(\bar X-h)]}{c\tau^2}. } \]
Known preparation or readout bias must enlarge the statistical radius. Rate and hopping uncertainty must be propagated separately.
Take
\[ t=1,\qquad d_{\mathrm{target}}=2,\qquad d_{\mathrm{baseline}}=16,\qquad \Lambda=4, \]
and perform
\[ N=100{,}000,\qquad \tau=\frac14. \]
If
\[ \boxed{\bar X\ge0.51,} \]
then the rationally checked confidence calculation gives, with confidence exceeding \(99\%\) conditional on the physical-model and calibration assumptions,
\[ D_{\mathrm{target}} \ge\frac{4950}{12679}>0.3904, \]
and
\[ \boxed{ \frac{D_{\mathrm{target}}}{D_{\mathrm{baseline}}} \ge \frac{39600}{12679}>3.12. } \]
The procedure may return inconclusive. Failure to cross the threshold does not certify poor transport.
A synthetic Bernoulli test passed this threshold. No physical experiment was performed.
The native evolution cost in this example is \(N\tau=25{,}000\) time units, plus every preparation, switching operation, reset, measurement and calibration. This is not a laboratory runtime estimate.
Preparing locally excited configurations requires work and control. Their cost is not an inverse Boltzmann occurrence probability, but it is not zero. Exact locality, translation invariance, the specified Markovian noise structure and the ability to freeze hopping are physical assumptions. One local assay cannot rule out arbitrary distant defects or unmodelled interactions.
Thus the rare-information barrier is avoided through an explicit additional intervention interface—not by smuggling target-equilibrium preparation into an oracle.
These comparisons are based on the respective primary sources. They do not establish an overall runtime advantage over those methods or over optimised tensor-network calculations. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.01859)
